panels.title: Up
panels.description: pg_up per server: 1 when the exporter can connect as lilnas_monitor and run its queries.

panels.title: Postgres version
panels.description: tdr-bot-db and icloud-backup-db run PG 18; immich-database runs PG 14 with VectorChord.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the database container started (cAdvisor container_start_time_seconds); Postgres is the container main process, so this is the postmaster uptime.

panels.title: Database size
panels.description: Size of the application database (tdr_bot, icloud_backup, immich).

panels.title: Connections used
panels.description: Backends across all databases as a share of max_connections (100 on all three servers). The exporter itself holds one or two.

panels.title: Deadlocks (range)
panels.description: Deadlocks detected over the selected time range.

panels.title: Rollbacks (range)
panels.description: Transactions rolled back over the selected time range. A few are normal (the exporter and ORMs roll back); a steady stream is not.

panels.title: Connections by state
panels.description: Backends per state (pg_stat_activity_count) with the max_connections ceiling as a dashed line.

panels.title: Transactions per second
panels.description: Commits and rollbacks per second, summed over all databases on each server.

panels.title: Rows fetched, inserted, updated, deleted
panels.description: Row operations per second, summed over all databases on each server.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Share of block requests served from shared buffers (blks_hit / (blks_hit + blks_read)). Gaps mean the server was idle in that window.

panels.title: Temp files created
panels.description: Temporary files per second written because a sort or hash spilled past work_mem. Zero is healthy.

panels.title: Temp bytes written
panels.description: Bytes per second written to temporary files. Zero is healthy.

panels.title: Database size over time
panels.description: Application database size per server (tdr_bot, icloud_backup, immich). Immich dwarfs the other two, so use the legend to isolate a series.

panels.title: Top 10 tables by size (per server)
panels.description: The ten largest tables on each selected server (table heap size, excluding indexes).

targets.expr: topk(10, pg_stat_user_tables_table_size_bytes{server="tdr-bot-db", server=~"$server"}) or topk(10, pg_stat_user_tables_table_size_bytes{server="icloud-backup-db", server=~"$server"}) or topk(10, pg_stat_user_tables_table_size_bytes{server="immich-database", server=~"$server"})

panels.title: Top 10 tables by dead tuples (per server)
panels.description: The ten tables with the most dead tuples on each selected server; autovacuum should keep these low.

targets.expr: topk(10, pg_stat_user_tables_n_dead_tup{server="tdr-bot-db", server=~"$server"}) or topk(10, pg_stat_user_tables_n_dead_tup{server="icloud-backup-db", server=~"$server"}) or topk(10, pg_stat_user_tables_n_dead_tup{server="immich-database", server=~"$server"})

panels.title: tdr-bot checkpointer tables
panels.description: The LangGraph checkpointer tables in tdr_bot (checkpoints, checkpoint_blobs, checkpoint_writes, checkpoint_migrations). Always shows tdr-bot-db, whatever the server variable says. checkpoint_blobs is the one that grows.

panels.title: tdr-bot checkpointer table size over time
panels.description: Heap size of each checkpointer table in tdr_bot. Ignores the server variable.

panels.title: Last autovacuum per table
panels.description: When autovacuum last ran on each table of the selected servers; "never" means it has not needed to yet.

panels.title: Locks by mode
panels.description: Locks held per mode (pg_locks_count), summed over databases.

panels.title: Longest running transaction
panels.description: Age of the oldest open transaction per server (pg_stat_activity_max_tx_duration). Idle-in-transaction sessions count.

panels.title: Idle in transaction and long-running
panels.description: Sessions idle in transaction, and transactions the long_running_transactions collector counts as long. Zero is healthy.

panels.title: WAL size
panels.description: Size of the pg_wal directory per server (pg_wal_size_bytes).

panels.title: Checkpoints per minute
panels.description: Timed and requested checkpoints. PG 14 reports them from pg_stat_bgwriter, PG 18 from pg_stat_checkpointer (needs the exporter stat_checkpointer collector, which is not enabled on the PG 18 exporters yet, so tdr-bot-db and icloud-backup-db are absent here until it is).

panels.title: Checkpoint write and sync time
panels.description: Milliseconds spent writing and syncing checkpoints per second. Same PG 14 / PG 18 split as Checkpoints per minute.

panels.title: Buffers written
panels.description: Buffers per second written by checkpoints (PG 14: buffers_checkpoint, PG 18: pg_stat_checkpointer buffers_written), by the background writer (buffers_clean) and allocated (buffers_alloc). The checkpoint line has the same PG 18 gap as Checkpoints per minute.

panels.title: Background writer stalls
panels.description: Times the background writer stopped a cleaning scan because it wrote too many buffers (maxwritten_clean). Exists on both PG 14 and PG 18; zero is healthy.

panels.title: Backend buffer writes (PG 14 only)
panels.description: Buffers written directly by backends instead of the checkpointer or bgwriter, and backend fsyncs. PG 14 reports these in pg_stat_bgwriter; PG 17 and later dropped them, so only immich-database appears.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU cores used by each database container (cAdvisor).

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Working set of each database container (cAdvisor).

panels.title: Disk I/O
panels.description: Block device reads (positive) and writes (negative) per second for each database container.

panels.title: Errors and fatals per server
panels.description: Event-driven: lines appear when Postgres logs ERROR, FATAL or PANIC (a failed query, a refused connection, a crash). A quiet database has none.

panels.title: Errors and fatals
panels.description: Event-driven: lines appear when Postgres logs ERROR, FATAL or PANIC. The exporter's own startup probes can log a few.
